intro: Six messages about work. Some are ordinary jobs, so refusing everything is not the skill. Decide, then look.
reflection: Which message were you least sure of, and which way would the money have moved?

sources.title: How to spot, avoid, and report fake check scams: personal assistant jobs are a named pattern, funds showing in your account do not make a check good, and you repay the bank when a fake is found weeks later (updated June 2025)
Job scams: honest employers never ask you to pay to get a job, and no honest employer sends a check to deposit and then asks you to send on part of the money (updated March 2023)
That job offer text is probably a scam: unexpected job messages by text, and never pay to get paid or to get a job (30 April 2026)
What to know about identity theft: someone using your details without permission can open accounts or get a job in your name (updated September 2024)

Searching for a job to work remotely? Avoid scams and identity theft: an interview in a text-only app, a quick 'you got the job', then direct deposit and tax forms asking for your bank account and personal information (13 November 2023)

Scammers impersonate well-known companies and recruit for fake jobs on job platforms: after the offer they push for your Social Security or bank account number for 'employment paperwork' (8 August 2023)
I-9 Central, completing Section 2: documents within three business days of starting work, and the employee chooses one List A document or one List B plus one List C (updated 18 September 2026)
Hiring employees: employers complete Form I-9 for every hire and ask for a signed Form W-4 when work starts (updated 18 February 2026)

lines: You're hired as a personal assistant.
We mailed you a check for $3,160.
Keep $260 and pay the rest to our event supplier through a payment app.

check.q: You deposited it, and the money shows in your banking app the next day. What do you do?

options.text: Send the $2,900, since the money has arrived
options.why: Money showing in your banking app does not make the check good. Found fake weeks later, it comes back and you owe the bank $2,900.

options.text: Send half now, and the rest once it clears
options.why: Whatever you send is your own money once the check bounces, and the whole $3,160 comes back off your balance.

options.text: Send nothing, and tell your bank the check may be fake
options.why: No real employer sends a check for you to pay on. Funds showing in your account do not make it a good check.

lines: Great chat. You're hired, no call needed.
Send your Social Security number and online banking login for direct deposit.

check.q: The job looked real on a big job site. What do you do?

options.text: Stop, and check the job through the company's own contact details
options.why: Hired by text with no call, and asked for a banking login, which no employer needs.

options.text: Send them, since payroll needs both
options.why: Direct deposit needs an account number on a form, never your login. With the login, someone else controls your account.

options.text: Send only the Social Security number
options.why: Sent to a stranger, it can be used for identity theft. Check the employer before any form asks for it.

lines: Library assistant, $15 an hour, 10 hours a week.
Paid through the college payroll every two weeks.
Form I-9: bring your documents within three business days of starting.
You choose which ones, from the list on the form.

check.q: You interviewed at the library desk on Monday. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, and bring the documents in your first days
options.why: An interview in person, pay from the college payroll, and the forms after the offer.

options.text: Refuse, since it asks for documents
options.why: Every employer completes Form I-9 with each new hire, after the offer. You pick the documents.
